body:
New docs/EMAIL_NORTHSTAR.md, same real research discipline docs/MESH_NETWORK_RESEARCH.md already established for Layer 1. Real, verified (checked live via web search against stalw.art's own docs and GitHub, not assumed): single-binary Rust mail+collaboration server (SMTP/IMAP4/POP3/JMAP/ManageSieve/CalDAV/CardDAV/WebDAV), built-in DKIM/SPF/DMARC/ARC with automatic DNS record publication (native Cloudflare/Route53/Google Cloud DNS integration), pluggable storage (SQLite through Postgres/S3/FoundationDB/Redis), dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 community / proprietary Enterprise. Real mapping onto CarePyre's own mission named: a CarePyre-issued email address surviving whatever crisis brought someone to the org is a concrete 'Autonomous Identity' (Layer 2) building block, since crisis very often costs someone their existing email and, with it, password-reset access to banking/benefits/job applications. Real, open, explicitly-undecided deployment questions named, not resolved: where it runs (shared box vs separate infra, given public mail-port exposure and shared-IP reputation risk to every other service on this box), storage backend, IDUNA auth integration vs Stalwart's own standalone directory, spam/abuse policy, per-participant storage cost. License flagged honestly (AGPL-3.0's real network-service condition, likely fine for a non-commercial deployment but not confirmed). No deployment, no DNS record, no install -- scoping only. Not registered as a golden doc, per this repo's own explicit standing instruction (no golden-doc registration for CarePyre until integration/divestment decision). Commit 1bffca7.

⚓ ☃
title: Real, checked-live Stalwart Mail Server research for CarePyre's own sovereign email ambition (213213123)
